what: AerCap is the world's largest aircraft leasing company. It buys aircraft, engines and helicopters and leases them to airlines, which prefer leasing to tying up capital in planes. It owns or manages about 3,500 assets.
customers: Airlines worldwide, which lease narrowbody and widebody aircraft, regional jets, freighters and engines.
money: engine leasing through Shannon Engine Support and helicopter leasing
gains on selling aircraft and fees for managing others' fleets
moat: Scale that gives it the best order positions with Boeing and Airbus and the lowest funding costs in the industry, in a business where cost of capital is the whole game.
risks: Debt of about $43 billion, though that is normal for a leasing company
Airline failures leave it repossessing aircraft
Interest rate rises raise its funding costs faster than lease rates reset
It lost a large fleet to the Russian seizure after 2022
opportunities: Aircraft shortages from Boeing and Airbus delays have pushed lease rates sharply higher
Net margin of 44% with consistent gains on aircraft sales
Large buybacks have shrunk the share count substantially
watch: Lease rate factors on new placements and book value per share.
